newsitem.title: USA: Counseling, condoms cut AIDS among couples - study.
newsitem.headline: Counseling, condoms cut AIDS among couples - study.

text.p: Low-tech solutions such as counselling and free condoms have a good chance of keeping the heterosexual partners of AIDS patients from getting infected, the National Institutes of Health reported on Monday.

Citing a study of 475 Haitian couples in which one partner was infected with the AIDS virus and the other was not, the institutes found that nearly half of the sexually active couples who got counselling and condoms practised safe sex.

In addition, the rate of new infections with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, among couples who consistently used condoms was one-seventh as high as it was among those who did not, according to the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, part of the NIH.
